page: Microsoft Azure F8ams_v6 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famsv6 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The instance features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs, utilizing a single thread per core configuration under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, though it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing performance is highly competitive, ranking in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core execution, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core benchmarks, falls within the average range. Memory performance shows a distinct tradeoff: while cached small-block read bandwidth and large-block write bandwidth are average, large-block uncached read bandwidth is weak, placing in the bottom 25%.

Given its high memory density and strong single-thread capabilities, the F8ams_v6 is suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and text processing tasks. It also supports vector and cryptography instructions, including AVX-512 and AES, which assist in cryptographic and integer manipulation tasks. The lack of local storage requires external storage attachment, which should be factored into the overall resource architecture. The dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable compute performance for workloads that do not require GPU acceleration.
